examples.en: The party primary is held next week.
He won the primary and became the candidate.
I am waiting for the primary results.
The two candidates competed fiercely in the primary.
I joined the party to take part in the primary.
The leader is chosen through a primary.

explain: '경선'은 후보를 정하는 선거이고, 그 뒤에 치르는 선거는 '본선'이라고 해요. '경선을 치르다', '경선에서 이기다'처럼 써요. 일반 투표를 말하는 '선거'와는 구별해서 써요.
explain_en: '경선' is the election to pick a candidate, and the election held afterward is the '본선'. Common phrases are '경선을 치르다' (hold a primary) and '경선에서 이기다' (win the primary). It is kept separate from '선거', the general word for an election.

examples.ko: 폭설 때문에 산골 마을이 이틀 동안 고립됐어요.
examples.en: The mountain village was cut off for two days because of heavy snow.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 무인도에 고립된 사람들 이야기예요.
examples.en: That movie is about people stranded on a deserted island.

examples.ko: 친구가 없어서 학교에서 혼자 고립되는 느낌이에요.
examples.en: I have no friends, so I feel isolated at school.
The bridge collapsed, and the village almost got cut off.
To avoid becoming isolated, talk with people often.

examples.ko: 길이 막혀서 차 안에 몇 시간 고립돼 있었어요.
examples.en: The road was blocked, so I was stuck in the car for hours.

explain: 마을이나 섬 같은 장소가 다른 곳과 끊길 때도, 사람이 주변과 관계가 끊길 때도 써요. '외롭다'는 마음의 느낌이고 '고립되다'는 놓인 상황이에요. 보통 피동형으로 쓰고, 일부러 그렇게 만들면 '고립시키다'예요.
explain_en: It works for places cut off from others, like villages and islands, and for people cut off from those around them. '외롭다' is a feeling, while '고립되다' describes the situation. It is usually used in the passive; doing it to someone on purpose is '고립시키다'.

examples.ko: 그 가수가 갑자기 인기 스타로 급부상했어요.
examples.en: That singer suddenly rose to become a popular star.

examples.ko: 새로운 기술의 급부상이 시장을 바꾸고 있어요.
examples.en: The sudden rise of the new technology is changing the market.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 우승 후보로 급부상하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team is suddenly emerging as a title contender.

examples.ko: 이 동네는 맛집 거리로 급부상한 곳이에요.
examples.en: This neighborhood is a place that has suddenly become a famous food street.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 그 회사의 급부상을 크게 다뤘어요.
examples.en: The news covered that company's sudden rise at length.

examples.ko: 작년에 급부상한 배우가 올해는 영화에 나와요.
examples.en: The actor who suddenly rose to fame last year appears in a movie this year.

explain: 주로 '급부상하다'로 써요. 사람, 회사, 나라가 짧은 시간에 눈에 띄게 올라올 때 쓰고, 뉴스에서 자주 들려요. 천천히 올라오면 '성장하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Mostly used as the verb 급부상하다. It is common in the news for a person, company or country that stands out in a short time. For slower growth, 성장하다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: Taxes and insurance premiums were deducted from the salary.

examples.ko: 연말정산에서 공제 항목을 꼼꼼히 챙기면 환급을 더 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you carefully claim every deduction at year-end tax settlement, you can get a bigger refund.

examples.ko: 부양가족이 있으면 인적 공제를 받을 수 있습니다.
examples.en: If you have dependents, you can receive a personal deduction.

examples.ko: 신용카드 사용액은 일정 금액을 넘으면 공제 대상이 됩니다.
examples.en: Credit card spending becomes eligible for a deduction once it exceeds a certain amount.

examples.ko: 공제 한도를 넘은 금액은 더 이상 혜택을 받지 못해요.
examples.en: Amounts over the deduction limit no longer get any benefit.

explain: 공제(控除)는 정해진 금액에서 일부를 빼는 일이에요. 월급에서 세금을 빼는 것도 공제, 세금 계산에서 혜택으로 빼 주는 것도 공제라서 문맥을 봐야 해요.
explain_en: 공제 (控除) means taking a portion off a set amount. Taking tax out of your pay is 공제, and so is the tax break that lowers your taxable amount, so you need the context.

examples.en: The police sealed off the accident scene.
It snowed a lot, so they close off the mountain road.
The government may seal the border.
They sealed off the entrance and evacuated people.

examples.ko: 도로를 봉쇄하는 바람에 차가 못 지나갔어요.
examples.en: Because the road was blocked off, cars could not pass.

examples.ko: 병원이 건물을 봉쇄해서 아무도 못 들어가요.
examples.en: The hospital sealed the building, so no one can enter.

explain: 봉쇄하다는 길, 문, 국경을 막아서 드나들지 못하게 할 때 써요. 뉴스에서 '도로 봉쇄', '국경 봉쇄'처럼 자주 보여요. 그냥 문을 닫는 건 '닫다', 길을 막는 건 '막다'를 써요.
explain_en: 봉쇄하다 is for blocking roads, doors or borders so nobody can get in or out. News often shows '도로 봉쇄' and '국경 봉쇄'. Simply closing a door is '닫다' and blocking a road is '막다'.

examples.en: The enemy's surprise attack began at night.
Everyone was shocked by the sudden attack.

examples.ko: 곰의 습격을 받은 마을 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard a story about a village hit by a bear attack.

examples.ko: 경찰은 은행 습격 사건을 조사하고 있어요.
examples.en: The police are investigating the bank raid.
The attack was over within a few minutes.
This movie starts with an alien attack.

explain: '습격을 받다', '습격을 당하다', '습격을 막다'처럼 써요. 사람, 동물, 군대가 갑자기 공격할 때 쓰고, 미리 알린 싸움에는 쓰지 않아요. 뉴스와 영화에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: Say '습격을 받다', '습격을 당하다' or '습격을 막다'. It fits sudden attacks by people, animals or armies, not a fight announced in advance. You hear it often in news and movies.

examples.en: That drama created a craze nationwide.
The idol craze spread overseas.
The news introduced a new craze.
My grandmother didn't know what a syndrome was.

examples.ko: 피로 신드롬을 앓는 직장인이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: The number of office workers suffering from fatigue syndrome is growing.

examples.ko: 한동안 그 노래는 거의 신드롬 수준이었어요.
examples.en: For a while, that song was almost at craze level.

explain: 의학에서는 여러 증상이 함께 나타나는 상태를 '증후군'이라고 하고, 일상에서는 사회적으로 크게 유행하는 현상을 '신드롬'이라고 해요. 그래서 '○○ 신드롬을 일으키다'가 많이 쓰여요. 비슷한 '열풍'은 뜨거운 인기를 강조해요.
explain_en: In medicine the Korean term is 증후군, while in daily life 신드롬 means a phenomenon that sweeps through society. A typical use is ○○ 신드롬을 일으키다. 열풍 is similar but stresses the heat of popularity.

en: to cause; to bring about; to lead to

examples.ko: 이 문제는 큰 혼란을 야기할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This problem could cause great confusion.
A small mistake led to an accident.
Excessive dieting brings about health problems.
That remark caused controversy, so he apologized.

examples.ko: 소음이 이웃 간의 갈등을 야기하기도 해요.
examples.en: Noise can sometimes cause conflict between neighbors.

examples.ko: 오해를 야기하지 않도록 정확하게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please speak precisely so as not to cause misunderstanding.

explain: 주로 문제, 갈등, 혼란, 논란처럼 좋지 않은 결과를 일으킬 때 써요. 일상에서는 '일으키다'를 쓰고, '야기하다'는 글이나 뉴스, 발표에서 많이 나와요. 소리가 비슷한 '이야기'와는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for causing unwelcome results such as problems, conflict, confusion and controversy. In daily talk people say '일으키다', while '야기하다' appears in writing, news and presentations. It is a different word from '이야기' (story), though they sound alike.

en: to be taken over; to be acquired (a company, business, or duty)

examples.en: That company was acquired by a large corporation.
The small shop changed its name when it was taken over.
Even after the takeover, the staff work as before.
I want to stop it from being acquired by a rival.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 작년에 다른 회사에 인수돼서 서비스가 달라졌어요.
examples.en: This app was acquired by another company last year, and its service changed.
Before it was acquired, it was running at a loss.

explain: '인수하다'는 사는 쪽, '인수되다'는 넘어가는 회사가 주어예요. 보통 '~에/에게 인수되다'로 써요. 뉴스에서 '대기업에 인수됐다'처럼 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: With '인수하다' the buyer is the subject; with '인수되다' the company being taken over is. It usually appears as '~에/에게 인수되다'. In the news you may hear '대기업에 인수됐다'.

examples.en: When the rain stopped, the suspended game was resumed.
Bus service will resume next week.
When will the stalled negotiations resume?

examples.ko: 점검이 끝나서 서비스가 곧 재개될 거예요.
examples.en: The check is done, so the service will resume soon.

examples.ko: 공사가 재개되면 소음이 다시 심해질 것 같아요.
examples.en: If the construction resumes, the noise will probably get bad again.

examples.ko: 오래 막혔던 대화가 아직도 재개되지 않았어요.
examples.en: The long-blocked talks still haven't resumed.

explain: 멈췄던 일이 다시 이어질 때만 써요. 처음 시작하는 일에는 쓰지 않아요. 공사, 협상, 운행, 경기 같은 말과 자주 나오고, 하는 사람이 있으면 '재개하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is only used when something that stopped starts again, never for a first start. It often goes with construction, negotiations, service and games. When someone does it on purpose, use the active form '재개하다'.

examples.en: The people rebuilt the collapsed bridge.
The government plans to rebuild the city.

examples.ko: 마을을 재건하는 데 오 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took five years to rebuild the village.
Everyone worked hard to rebuild the company.

examples.ko: 불에 탄 절을 재건해서 다시 열었어요.
examples.en: They rebuilt the temple that burned down and reopened it.

examples.ko: 폐허 위에 마을을 재건하고 학교도 세웠어요.
examples.en: They rebuilt the village on the ruins and put up a school too.

explain: 무너지거나 없어진 큰 것을 새로 세울 때 써요. 건물뿐 아니라 회사, 나라, 삶에도 써요. 작은 물건은 '고치다'를 쓰고, 부서진 것을 원래대로 되돌리는 일은 '복구하다'를 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Use it for raising something big that collapsed or disappeared. It works for buildings and also for companies, countries and lives. Small items are just '고치다', and restoring something broken to its original state is more often '복구하다'.

examples.en: A big tragedy was reported on the news.
Many people were hurt in that tragedy.
The government is investigating the cause of the disaster.

examples.ko: 다시는 이런 참사가 일어나지 않아야 해요.
examples.en: A tragedy like this must never happen again.
People laid flowers at the site of the tragedy.

examples.ko: 그 참사를 잊지 않으려고 기념식을 열어요.
examples.en: They hold a memorial ceremony so that the tragedy is not forgotten.

explain: 참사는 사고나 사건으로 사람이 많이 죽거나 다친 끔찍한 일을 말해요. 뉴스에서는 '대형 참사', '참사 현장'처럼 나오고, 가벼운 사고에는 쓰지 않아요. '일어나다', '막다'와 함께 자주 써요.
explain_en: 참사 refers to a terrible event in which many people are killed or hurt. In the news it appears as '대형 참사' and '참사 현장'. It is not used for minor accidents, and it often goes with '일어나다' and '막다'.

en: to be propelled; to be pushed; to be driven

examples.en: The new plan will be pushed forward from next month.

examples.ko: 공원 만드는 일이 빠르게 추진되고 있어요.
examples.en: The park project is moving ahead quickly.
That project was driven by the city.
The plan went ahead as scheduled.
The work couldn't move forward for lack of money.
It is scheduled to go ahead within this year.

explain: '추진되다'는 계획이나 사업이 실제로 진행될 때 써요. '계획이 추진되다', '사업이 추진되다'처럼 계획이나 정책이 주어예요. 뉴스와 공문에서 많이 보여요. 사람이 하면 '계획을 추진하다'예요.
explain_en: 추진되다 is used when a plan or project actually goes forward. Plans and policies are the subject, as in '계획이 추진되다'. It shows up a lot in news and official documents. When a person does it, use '계획을 추진하다'.

examples.en: Everyone hopes a nuclear war won't break out.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 핵전쟁 이후의 세상을 보여 줘요.
examples.en: That movie shows the world after a nuclear war.
I watched a news report on the danger of nuclear war.

examples.ko: 핵전쟁이 나면 지구 전체가 위험해질 거예요.
examples.en: If a nuclear war breaks out, the whole Earth will be in danger.

examples.ko: 여러 나라가 핵전쟁을 막으려고 회담을 열었어요.
examples.en: Several countries held talks to prevent nuclear war.
In class we learned about the damage of nuclear war.

explain: '핵전쟁이 일어나다/나다', '핵전쟁을 막다/피하다'로 자주 써요. '핵'은 원자핵에서 온 말로 '핵무기', '핵발전소'에도 붙어요. 뉴스와 토론에서 주로 나오는 말이라 일상 대화에서는 가볍게 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Common patterns are '핵전쟁이 일어나다/나다' and '핵전쟁을 막다/피하다'. '핵' comes from the atomic nucleus and is also in '핵무기' and '핵발전소'. It mostly appears in news and debates, so it isn't used casually in everyday talk.
